pros: Identifies natural community boundaries via edge betweenness
Produces interpretable hierarchical dendrogram of communities
Principled measure: edges with high betweenness are natural bridges
No prior knowledge of number of communities required
Works on both directed and undirected graphs
Modularity Q provides objective criterion for best partition
Intuitive divisive approach mirrors graph connectivity structure
Detects communities at multiple scales simultaneously
Theoretically elegant: bridges graph theory and community structure
cons: Computationally expensive: O(V × E²) limits to small/medium graphs
Impractical for graphs with > 10⁴ nodes in most implementations
Must recompute betweenness after every single edge removal
Multiple edges may tie for highest betweenness (ambiguity)
Edge betweenness is expensive to compute precisely
Requires all-pairs shortest paths in each iteration
Cannot detect overlapping communities (hard partitions only)
Shortest path assumption may not hold for all networks
Removal of single edge can drastically change betweenness values
May fragment graph into many tiny components before optimal Q found
No theoretical guarantee of optimal modularity
